info.bio:
The Nitty Gritty Dirt Band se formó en el sur de California durante la primavera de 1966, como una joven banda desaliñada. Cuarenta y dos años mas tarde, el cuarteto (Jeff Hanna, Jimmie Fadden, Bob Carpenter y John McEuen) sigue activo.

El album autotitulado de The Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, lanzado en 1967, incluye el éxito “buy me for the rain”. Pero fue su quinta grabación, "Uncle Charlie and His Dog Teddy " de 1970, la que se convertiría en el proyecto revelación

scenes.name: Country-rock y roots-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En los setenta, el reajuste a los viejos valores (blues, folk, country) convierte al rock en uno de los mayores éxitos del consumismo: el Establishment ya no intenta destruirlo, lo absorbe. El country-rock de Gram Parsons es una moda enorme: Commander Cody, New Riders Of The Purple Sage, Manassas, Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, Poco y los Eagles (Desperado, Hotel California); en Nashville surgen los «outlaws» (Waylon Jennings, Willie Nelson, Kris Kristofferson). El roots-rock sigue con Hot Tuna, Little Feat y Doobie Brothers, y la nostalgia recupera el blues (Roy Buchanan, Bonnie Raitt), la armonía vocal (Manhattan Transfer, Roches, McGarrigle Sisters) y los cincuenta (American Graffiti).

podcast.title: Fiddle Accompanied Spoken Word (1974)
podcast.body: The Nitty Gritty Dirt Band, fitting into the country rock genre, recorded a spoken word version of Stephen Vincent Benét's poem "The Mountain Whippoorwill" with fiddle accompaniment on their 1974 album "Stars and Stripes Forever." This recording contains the "seeds" of "The Devil Went Down to Georgia" by The Charlie Daniels Band. "The nitty gritty dirt band who also would fit into this kind of country rock genre. They did a spoken word. I guess would be the best way to put it recording of that same poem with fiddle accompaniment on their stars and stripes forever album which came out in 74."

podcast.title: First American Band to Tour Soviet Union (1977)
podcast.body: In 1977, the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band was chosen over more conventional acts like the Doobie Brothers and America to be the first American band to tour the Soviet Union. This tour, endorsed by President Jimmy Carter, aimed to undermine communism through rock and roll. The tour proved immensely successful among young people in Russia and other Soviet republics, generating such high demand for tickets that it overwhelmed the KGB. "To be the first American band to tour through the Soviet Union, President Jimmy Carter was all for this, thinking that rock and roll could undermine communism."

podcast.title: Kansas City Heroes
podcast.body: Rock journalism legend Greg Shaw regarded the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band as heroes in Kansas City, a city he noted was not a major rock music center, yet fans there were devoted and willing to travel for their music. Shaw also identified Kansas City as the "spiritual home of country rock." "Greg Shaw wrote that the nitty gritty dirt band that they were considered heroes in Kansas City, which he rightly noted, was not a major rock music center, but fans of the region knew what they liked and they were willing to travel to hear it."

concerts.title: 1977 Soviet Union Tour
concerts.body: The Nitty Gritty Dirt Band was selected over the Doobie Brothers and the soft rock band America to become the first American band to tour the Soviet Union in 1977. This tour, championed by President Jimmy Carter who believed rock and roll could undermine communism, was a wild success among young people in Russia and various Soviet republics, with demand for tickets overwhelming the KGB. "In 1977, the nitty-gritty dirt band was chosen over the Dubie brothers, and the soft rock band America, must have been their name, to be the first American band to tour through the Soviet Union."

xref.title: Considered for Soviet Tour
xref.body: The Doobie Brothers were considered as potential candidates for the first American band to tour the Soviet Union in 1977 but were ultimately passed over in favor of the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band. This initiative was part of a US effort to use rock and roll to undermine communism through cultural exchange. "In 1977, the nitty-gritty dirt band was chosen over the Dubie brothers, and the soft rock band America, must have been their name, to be the first American band to tour through the Soviet Union."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Considered for Soviet Tour
xref.body: The soft rock band America was among the groups considered to be the first American band to tour the Soviet Union in 1977. However, the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band was ultimately selected for this cultural mission, which aimed to introduce American rock music into Soviet society as a form of soft power. "In 1977, the nitty-gritty dirt band was chosen over the Dubie brothers, and the soft rock band America, must have been their name, to be the first American band to tour through the Soviet Union."
